objective: Turn the existing talking-avatar hero into a playable third-person 3D portfolio world (Play button, campus with three portfolio destinations, collectible challenge, desktop and mobile controls, pause/exit/cleanup) while preserving the regular portfolio and the talking-avatar feature.

sred.technicalChallenge: Whether the existing Avaturn avatar and Mixamo-derived clips can be retargeted into a physics-driven locomotion state machine, and whether a hero-to-game transition can share one rendering canvas and avatar skeleton without the talking scene and the game scene competing for control, within the 60 FPS desktop / 30 FPS mobile and 8 MB additional-asset budgets.
sred.approachAndResult: Retargeted the existing Avaturn avatar to Mixamo-derived clips with a baked clothing fix and drove it with a Rapier fixed-step kinematic controller, sharing one React Three Fiber canvas between the talking hero and the game through a session state machine. Iterated over 12 QA rounds and 3 Codex cross-review rounds: slope and step handling, grounded landing, a sphere-cast follow camera with line-of-sight and body-clearance solving (round 1 of the final review found the camera could be pushed past the solved clear distance; fixed by bounding it and clipping the avatar with the near plane), worker-based procedural texture painting and batched shader warm-up. Result: 60 FPS (vsync-bound, render CPU p95 0.8 ms) on an M1 Pro at 1440x900 and 1920x1080 and under 4x CPU-throttled phone emulation, about 0.95 MB extra first-play download against an 8 MB budget, cold Play-to-swap cut from about 1.3 s to 0.7 s, no resource growth over 50 entry and exit cycles, and every failure row recovering to a usable portfolio; mobile performance on a physical device remains unmeasured.

acceptanceCriteria: Clicking Play transitions the existing avatar from the talking-avatar hero into the 3D world with a loading indicator and a working Cancel.
Walking, running, jumping, gravity, wall collision, slope and step handling, and a collision-aware third-person camera work with keyboard and mouse on desktop.
All three destinations (Project Lab, Skills Workshop, Contact Tower) are reachable on foot and present existing portfolio content from data/index.ts and lib/persona.ts without invented claims.

The three-cell collectible challenge can be completed, celebrated at the plaza beacon, and restarted; progress persists locally in a versioned format with safe fallback when storage is unavailable or corrupt.
Touch joystick, camera drag, jump and interact controls work on mobile viewports.

Pause, Exit, repeated entry and exit, tab-hide auto-pause, and load cancellation restore hero camera, idle avatar, page scroll, keyboard focus, and leave voice chat disconnected with the microphone released.
Ordinary portfolio browsing downloads no game-world, physics, or locomotion-only assets; game modules are not in the initial portfolio bundle.
Game failures (asset download, physics init, WebGL unavailable, context loss, invalid save) leave the regular portfolio usable.

Focused automated tests cover game-state transitions, load cancellation, input normalization and blur release, grounding and jump eligibility, collectible uniqueness, completion and restart, storage fallback, entry/exit cleanup, and project-panel focus handling, and they pass.
Build and lint pass, or every remaining failure is explicitly reported with its baseline status.
Performance is measured and recorded against named environments, distinguishing real-device runs from emulation.
The final code revision has independent cross-provider review (Claude-authored code reviewed by Codex), or the exact blocker is reported and no independent review is claimed.
A feature-branch pull request contains the implementation summary, verification evidence, cross-review evidence, screenshots or recordings where available, and known limitations.

Clicking Play is one continuous cinematic transition with no hard cut: the page chrome (nav, hero text, buttons, talk button, hints) animates out with a short staggered fade and slide, the hero canvas grows smoothly from its hero box to full screen, the camera moves from the hero framing to behind the avatar while the avatar turns and walks into the world, and loading progress, if assets are not ready yet, shows unobtrusively while the avatar idles instead of a blocking screen (the game chunk is prefetched on Play hover or focus); Exit plays the same sequence in reverse back to the exact hero layout; with prefers-reduced-motion the sequence becomes a short crossfade; the whole transition stays at the frame-rate budget and is verified with a recorded frame sequence.

Carried from M1 QA round 3 (user-approved deferral): during any drop, landing or camera drag in the campus, the avatar's head and torso are never hidden behind level geometry for any rendered frame (head-to-camera line-of-sight test against every camera-blocking collider) and the camera never goes below the ground surface at any pitch, each covered by automated tests that fail on the M1 camera code.

Carried from the Codex M1 cross-review: the follow camera enforces CAMERA.minDistance on pull-in (a sphere-cast hit closer than the minimum keeps the camera at the minimum view distance and never inside the avatar), covered by a boundary test that fails on the M1 camera code.
constraints: Stack: Next.js 14.1.4 App Router, React 18, TypeScript strict, three ^0.163, @react-three/fiber ^8, @react-three/drei ^9, Tailwind terminal palette; Node 22.x toolchain.
Reuse public/avatar.glb and the existing walk/run clips unless the Milestone 0 audit demonstrates a concrete rigging or visual-quality problem; preserve avatar identity.

Preserve the talking-avatar hero behavior (voice session, gestures, lip-sync, head mouse-follow) and the regular portfolio sections unchanged except for the Play entry point and shared avatar extraction.
Reuse portfolio content from data/index.ts and lib/persona.ts; never invent results, testimonials, or project claims; do not use data/index.ts testimonials (placeholders).
Keep game code, physics, and world assets out of the ordinary portfolio loading path (dynamic import after Play; no game imports from app/page.tsx or TalkingAvatar module scope).
Do not touch app/api/realtime-session/route.ts, lib/persona.ts content, OPENAI_API_KEY handling, next.config.mjs CSP except an additive wasm/worker entry if physics requires it (record it).
Pre-existing unrelated local changes on the primary checkout (README.md banner, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, upwork-profile.txt) are outside this task and must not be staged or altered.
No new paid services, accounts, or backend game services; no third-party assets without a recorded source and license.
All specialist work happens inside the per-task isolated worktree; every git/npm command is scoped to it.
Follow .claude/skills/engineering-excellence/SKILL.md and development-workflow; one implementation owner (game-dev) per milestone with graphics-engineer only for rendering-specific deliverables.
outOfScope: Multiplayer, combat, vehicles, character customization, procedurally generated terrain.
Replacing the voice/Realtime integration or editing persona text.
Consolidating duplicate next.config / postcss config files (board backlog item).
Real iOS/Android device testing beyond devices actually available on this machine (reported as gaps, not claimed).
Sound, sound toggle and volume, and user-selectable quality presets (deferred by user decision on 2026-10-07 to save time and tokens; recorded as a follow-up).

decisions.decision: Bake the clothing fix into public/avatar.glb offline instead of applying it at runtime: the runtime version was a 264 to 973 ms main-thread task deferred 5 to 8 s after load, causing a visible switch from flawed to fixed shirt. Asset change is limited to clothing data under the user's approval to fix the hero shirt.

Visual fix round (reports/23-graphics-engineer-visual-fix.json): accepted the entry fade with a largest luminance step of 6.8 to 7.0 (2.27x the 10-neighbour median) because the steps form a monotone ramp (5.6, 6.8, 6.2, 5.4, 4.0, 3.0, 2.3) after the swap, not a pop, and the neighbour median is depressed by static pre-fade frames; QA judges it by eye. Accepted the about 1.1 s longer cold load caused by frame-budgeted procedural texture painting, with starting texture generation at prefetch time (Play hover or focus) assigned to the Milestone 5 performance pass. Faint residual interior wall streaks are recorded as a known limitation for M5 polish.
